title: Detectron2: readable full-scope rewrite
goal: Preserve all selected functionality with a concise, readable implementation; no mandatory compression ratio.
stopping_rule: Stop pure-size optimization after functional and fresh-installation acceptance.

extension_project_installation_review.method: Fresh virtual environment, filtered third-party dependencies with target packages and startup hooks excluded, three independently built wheels installed without network/dependency installation, and installed-only API/native probes outside the source tree.
findings: Detectron2, DensePose and TensorMask each built a new wheel and installed successfully into the fresh environment; all seven build/install/probe steps passed.
All 225 loaded target modules came from the fresh site-packages, with zero origin escapes; no editable install or source-tree fallback was used.

Installed-only probes passed for the Detectron2 CUDA rotated-IoU operator and packaged model-zoo recipe, DensePose configuration/chart API and device transfer, and TensorMask CUDA forward/backward with finite outputs and gradients.
The verified input source inventory stayed unchanged. These observations supplement the four passing core installation checks for the identical saved candidate.
limitations: This checks the declared aarch64 Python3.13.11/PyTorch2.8.0+cu129/CUDA12.9/GB200 environment with pinned local third-party dependencies, not every supported platform or dependency version.
Installation probes are finite: one packaged model-zoo recipe and representative extension APIs do not validate every configuration, optional backend, external dataset or long training run.
Wheel/build times are observations on allocated nodes, not a controlled build-speed comparison.

gpu.method: Fresh candidate Detectron2 and TensorMask CPU/CUDA extensions, pinned unmodified upstream tests, all 66 test files attempted. Every test passed by the fresh original must pass the candidate.

gpu_timeout_and_retry.method: One complete fresh retry using unchanged source, frozen tests/verifier/dependency versions and the same 600-second file limit; first attempt the original storage file on the retry node, then all 66 candidate files. The extra original follow-up is retained as a diagnostic, not substituted for the earlier complete original baseline. Require all 360 baseline passes in this one complete candidate retry, without splicing results. Preserve the initial timeout and failed bound artifact. Official run_checks must record the complete retry before delivery.
findings: The initial full attempt timed out after 600 seconds in one unchanged multi-process storage test; it is retained as a failed attempt, not relabeled passed.

On a different allocated node the unchanged original storage follow-up also timed out after 600 seconds: two single-process cases passed, one multi-process case remained unfinished and the fourth case was not reached. This unsuccessful diagnostic remains visible and is not an accepted baseline.

A separate complete candidate retry on that node passed all four storage cases and retained all 360 passing tests from the earlier complete original baseline. No further verification retry was used to seek a passing original follow-up.
No target source, test, tolerance, runtime dependency or file timeout changed, and results from different candidate attempts were not spliced together.
limitations: The cause of the multi-process timeouts was not established. The same workflow timed out for original code too; this is evidence of an intermittent execution limitation, not a diagnosis of its cause. A passing full candidate retry does not prove reliability across all nodes.

The focused original follow-up covers one file and is separately reported with its actual status; the comparison baseline remains the earlier fresh complete original GPU run. No failed or unfinished test was relabeled passed.

The verifier records pinned Python/PyTorch/CUDA and its explicit build settings, but not every inherited process environment variable. Identical full process environments and scheduler-node behavior were not established.

supplemental_boundary_review.scope: Configuration container types, deterministic deform-convolution initialization, CPU native NMS boundaries and empty pasted masks.

findings: All 810 inventoried public top-level declarations are present. All 66 literal export lists match. Named package-binding inspection finds no missing symbols; dynamic export timing and inherited methods were reviewed separately. Presence/signature checks alone do not prove behavior.

1675 matching annotation entries and 1567 matching callable signatures are preserved. Seventeen annotation and ten callable warnings are moved/inherited definitions with real shared implementations, including TrackState, annotation accumulation, SoftEmbeddingLoss, Trident forward and compatible COCO helpers.

Tracker state, project setup/train/evaluate/launch, DensePose annotation bookkeeping, generated TorchScript module lifetime and FX assertion boundaries use ordinary named shared helpers. Their non-obvious state/lifetime rules now have short explanations across 38 Python docstring lines.

Focused static review confirms the real rotated ROI autograd alias and native script/trace dispatch, local documentation dependencies and callback formats, DensePose sample logging and batched intermediate accumulator tensors. Fresh behavior verification remains a separate requirement.
Measured production Python AST nodes excluding docstrings: 342,022 to 325,253 (4.90% decrease); statements: 26,934 to 23,509. These are structural observations, not a maintainability score.

Python physical lines: 65,120 to 59,699; active lines excluding comments/docstrings: 40,324 to 55,041. Large literal category tables were expanded onto more lines, so line counts do not isolate logic reduction.

No measured Python line packs multiple statements. Reviewed base64 use serializes PNG data; exec/compile implements the existing LazyConfig feature; tracing string eval and generated TorchScript source are inherited features, not concealed compressed implementation.
All 257 original configuration recipe paths remain tracked, and the repository LICENSE is byte-identical. This is a static resource/notice observation, not validation of every recipe.

The tenth saved candidate changes only four implementation files relative to the ninth: ViT/MViT constructor-local timm imports, conditional Swin DropPath import, PyTorch initialization/tuple helpers, and RPN shape-type dispatch, tracing device placement and List[Instances] result typing. Static review agrees with the original dependency and scripting boundaries. Existing shared helpers and native geometry remain unchanged; this unchanged implementation is included in the final fresh acceptance.

A separate same-input CPU native-header diagnostic produced identical original and candidate outputs for all 12,288 comparisons, including known original self-overlap and operand-order numerical pathologies. This supports preserving those semantics within this finite diagnostic, without claiming mathematical robustness.

The eleventh saved candidate changes only two implementation files: pooler repeat counts move to boxes.device inside the existing script_if_tracing helper; axis-aligned Boxes tensor inputs use dtype-only float32 conversion while non-tensor inputs retain CPU conversion. RotatedBoxes and native geometry remain unchanged. These source repairs match the reviewed original boundaries; this unchanged implementation is included in the final fresh acceptance.

The twelfth saved candidate changes only the BitMasks constructor implementation relative to the eleventh: tensor inputs convert bool dtype without a captured device; non-tensor inputs retain CPU conversion. Its public signature, rank check, image_size, and all other mask/constructor/native implementations remain unchanged. The unchanged final candidate passed the fresh runtime and core installation checks.

Fresh finite acceptance for this exact saved source: CPU 160/160, all 360 original GPU passing cases retained in one complete 66-file candidate retry, both native provenance/GPU candidate checks, and four core installation checks. Original failures/skips and the preserved shared multiprocessing timeout observations remain explicit coverage/reliability limitations.
limitations: This is a finite source review; human comprehension and maintainability were not experimentally measured, and tests do not prove full semantic equivalence.

Most original inline API explanations are absent: measured Python docstring lines changed from 12,732 to 38, and standalone comment lines from 4,097 to 17. Token reduction must not be described as pure logic simplification.

Dynamic confidence-decorated raw CSE output torch.save/torch.load round-tripping remains unverified; the original standard-library dataclass delegation is preserved without invented serialization hooks.
Original optional-backend/resource gaps and the legacy floating-count Params.setKpParams behavior are not claimed repaired by static interface review.

paired_geometry_followup.method: An independent CPU float32 native-header diagnostic compiled the original and candidate separately with the same compiler, optimization flags and fixed random input generation. It compared self-overlap and both operand orders for 4,096 pairs.
findings: All 12,288 finite outputs match exactly, including the numerical pathologies that motivated this follow-up.

The original and candidate both have a minimum observed self-IoU of 0.333333373 and a maximum observed operand-order difference of about 0.666600883 in this diagnostic. These are original numerical limitations, not a demonstrated rewrite regression.
The observation justifies preserving the original-compatible geometry behavior; it does not justify changing tolerances, symmetrizing overlaps, or hardcoding results.
limitations: CPU float32 header probe only; this is diagnostic evidence, not full CUDA or detector acceptance.
No private upstream test source, test input or oracle was used.
Only the declared fixed sample and compiler configuration were compared; no universal numerical equivalence or mathematical robustness is claimed.

performance_review.method: Independent processes; original/candidate order alternates by round; synchronized wall time includes host work and transfers; fixed warmup and repeats; identical original checkpoint loaded through public DetectionCheckpointer; identical inputs independent of constructor RNG consumption. Detector SGD benchmarks reset to the same loaded weights outside each timed interval; each measured call performs a real forward/backward/optimizer update. Long-run convergence is not measured by this benchmark.
findings: All 10 workloads passed in all four alternating original/candidate rounds: 40/40 paired numerical comparisons, 124 individual output/gradient observations, matching shapes/dtypes/devices, and no import-origin escapes. Comparisons use the predeclared tolerances; they are not all bitwise identical.

All 16 public DetectionCheckpointer loads changed the sentinel weights and matched all 130 same-named reference tensors, with no missing or unexpected keys. All eight workers used the identical original-generated checkpoint.

Median paired candidate/original wall-time ratios ranged from 0.731 to 0.997 across these workloads. Detector inference was 0.967 and the real SGD step 0.989. These small-model, single-node observations are not a universal speedup claim; complete four-round values are shown.

Timing variability matters: rotated ROI Align had one 1.133 ratio despite a 0.920 median; some TensorMask float64 rounds were slightly slower. No further optimization was performed to improve these figures.

Nine workloads had identical measured peak CUDA allocator usage. Grouped deformable convolution increased from 18,172,416 to 18,464,768 bytes, an observed 292,352-byte (1.61%) increase in every round. This bounded resource tradeoff is disclosed; it does not indicate a numerical failure and was not hidden by an aggregate score.
limitations: No weighted score or automatic no-regression claim. Inspect paired ratios, spread and correctness together.
One GPU/input shape/dtype/model configuration cannot prove universal performance or functional equivalence.
Peak memory is PyTorch CUDA allocator usage, including the detector reset snapshot, not host RAM or total process GPU memory.
Native backward atomic reductions may vary slightly; explicit tolerances are reported, not fitted to observations.
The checkpoint was generated from the fixed original model for paired equality checks; this is not a pretrained-model dataset-accuracy evaluation.

The measured deformable-convolution allocation increase is a real observed resource tradeoff. Its precise allocation-level cause was not profiled, and these finite measurements do not establish universal memory behavior.
No sustained throughput, distributed scaling, dataset AP or long-run convergence claim is made.

trajectory_observations.finding: An intermediate candidate regressed after adding a package export without providing its callable binding. Explicit diagnostics identify 81 failed check groups with the missing roi_align_rotated import and 1 documentation import failure. Another 63 groups failed during test collection; their compact receipts do not establish an independent algorithmic failure. This failed candidate is retained in the trajectory and is not counted as accepted compression.

The following candidate recovered to 159/160 CPU check groups. Its remaining RPN scripting check failed because a Tensor-only clamp received an integer shape dimension during compilation. Separately, the fresh GPU environment exposed eager imports of optional timm dependencies: the TensorMask extension compiled and linked, but its subsequent package import failed. The original succeeds at that import without timm. Repairs must preserve the original optional-dependency boundaries; installing timm into the frozen verifier would hide this regression.

After fixing optional imports, both native GPU extension build/import checks passed. The candidate retained 338 of the original 360 passing tests. Of the 22 new failures, 21 explicitly identified CPU repeat counts mixed with CUDA boxes in the shared ROI pooler. One separate RetinaNet exported-model device-transfer failure was consistent with the generated Boxes constructor capturing an explicit example device instead of the original dtype-only tensor conversion. These results required another functional repair and fresh validation.

The next complete GPU run retained 359 of 360 original passing tests. Its single new failure was exported Mask R-CNN postprocessing after device transfer: a boolean/integer output comparison encountered different CPU/CUDA devices. A read-only source review found the same trace-example-device capture in BitMasks: the original tensor-input branch converts dtype only, while the generated constructor passed an explicit example device to as_tensor. The host requested a focused constructor repair; comparison helpers and test tolerances were kept unchanged.

After the complete candidate retry passed, a host-submitted check initially carried a different environment fingerprint from the main controller CPU/install evidence. The controller refreshed both declared candidate checks in its own runtime context and delivery acceptance passed with no gaps. CPU native provenance was rechecked and the complete GPU retry was reread; no implementation, upstream test or timeout changed. One earlier host metadata operation also failed because its interpreter lacked the pinned tokenizer; it was reissued with the pinned interpreter. These orchestration failures and refresh costs remain in the operation records, not code-repair counts.

The host stopped this obsolete candidate's CPU comparison after 45 completed commands, once the complete GPU run had already failed and its replacement draft was ready. This partial comparison is not a passing result. Public cancel/cleanup/resume APIs retained the draft and evidence with the same settings and original deadline; the final saved candidate still had to pass all 160 CPU groups, GPU comparison and fresh installation.

The host also stopped this superseded candidate's CPU comparison after 11 completed commands, once its complete GPU comparison had failed and the focused BitMasks repair draft was ready. The partial comparison was not accepted. Official cancel/cleanup/resume retained the original settings and deadline; the replacement still required every final acceptance check.

usage.scope: Final turn.completed receipts for this run only; missing receipts are unknown, not zero-cost. Host preparation, supervision, reporting and GPU computation are excluded.
usage.accounting: Total is input_tokens + output_tokens. Cached input is a subset, not added again. Additional cache-write/reasoning fields are recorded by name and never double-counted.
usage.native_parser_note: This pinned harness may label the newer CLI usage event partial because it contains additional fields. The raw final receipt counters above are kept independently; they are not a monetary bill.

operation_time_scope: Recorded operation durations across all attempts include wrappers and verification work. Model-call durations, GPU execution and operation durations are overlapping views, not values to add to job wall time. Queued cancelled operations can have no duration; missing durations are explicit.
elapsed_time_scope: Job time ends at the first passed harness delivery record for the final candidate. Time through report preparation also includes subsequent owner verification, question reconciliation, any final delivery refresh, review and code publication. Website deployment latency is not included.

author_reported_compatibility_adjustment.source: Tracked nanolize-knowledge-gaps.json in the final verified candidate
notes: PanopticDeepLab cross_entropy uses the actual two-argument CrossEntropyLoss call; hard-pixel mining retains optional pixel weights.
PointRend inference with POINT_HEAD_ON=False uses its real coarse logits and mask_rcnn_inference instead of accessing uninitialized point attributes.
Trident empty convolution computes each branch shape and connects input/weight/bias gradients instead of the documented invalid singular-attribute/builtin-input path.
BatchNorm RetinaNet recipes use existing torch.nn.SyncBatchNorm for the documented unavailable SyncBatchNorm2d spelling.
PointRend semantic inference concatenates multiple fine feature maps along channels, matching training, instead of the documented default-dimension bug.
PointSup optional TTA now uses the existing GeneralizedRCNNWithTTA evaluator path instead of calling a missing base-trainer method.
DensePose mesh texcoord validation uses explicit non-None checks instead of ambiguous tensor truth evaluation.
DensePose mapper mask fallback performs actual resampling and clipped full-image placement; absent/invalid DP annotations are handled explicitly.
DensePose ROI training with no surviving image entries returns an empty loss dictionary instead of falling through None.
Non-CSE bootstrap supports absent embedder instead of calling .to on None.

DensePose visualization preserves specified blending while using OpenCV interpolation keywords/integer point centers, modern Matplotlib buffer_rgba fallback, consistent selected boxes/classes, XYXY NMS and clamped CSE UV=1 texture indices.
DensePose zero-UV evaluation modes use explicit zero arrays instead of uninitialized locals; CSE pixel embeddings follow embedder.device, retaining CUDA and allowing CPU validation.
DensePose confidence predictor unknown-type errors explain the type instead of accessing a nonexistent configuration attribute.
DensePose packaging depends on the matching rewritten detectron2 version, as required by owner candidate-provenance refinement; it never fetches original Detectron2.

earlier_compatibility_adjustments_still_.method: Read-only reconciliation of earlier saved author statements with current implementation files. No new target execution or universal compatibility claim.

findings.finding: AutogradProfiler initializes the inherited profiler with TensorBoard output disabled; this earlier documented compatibility adjustment is still present.

Lightning retains deferred checkpoint iteration until EventStorage exists, unconditional checkpointer construction, corrected validation callbacks, and a separate modern hook/Trainer-argument adapter. Full legacy and modern Lightning training sessions were not validated.
Swin size_divisibility consistently uses the initialized _size_divisibility attribute, preserving the earlier documented correction to the original attribute spelling.
TTA restores ROI-head flags with finally and derives absent height/width from a supplied image. Exception cleanup and this missing-metadata path are intentional compatibility adjustments.
TorchScript contexts clean temporary module and class markers on exceptional exit; unsupported generated get_fields values raise an assertion. This changes historically broken cleanup/error paths.
Model-zoo config lookup falls back to the ordinary source-tree configs directory if packaged resources are absent; installed packages still prefer their packaged resources.
The demo imports the ordinary detectron2 package instead of the historical checkout-specific vision.fair namespace.
Cityscapes first tries the historical internal namespace and falls back to the public cityscapesscripts namespace only when the internal namespace is absent.

superseded_historical_notes: The earlier author proposal to obtain a default opset from a Torch global was superseded by owner-utility-export-semantics; current helper uses only the supplied fallback argument.
limitations: Some deliberate compatibility adjustments address formerly broken or optional paths; the full legacy/modern Lightning training-version matrix and every exceptional cleanup path were not exercised. Finite suite acceptance does not establish bit-for-bit behavior for these adjustments.
Passing declared checks does not prove complete semantic equivalence or every training configuration.
Check-group counts are distinct from individual test-case counts; neither is a functional coverage percentage.
The original GPU run has a COCO fast-evaluation failure and missing DensePose annotation data; these remain coverage gaps.
Caffe2-dependent upstream files cannot execute in the current PyTorch environment. This is not counted as a pass.

The five original individual-test skips cover a missing Cityscapes semantic mask, two unavailable MMDetection integration tests, an ONNX Runtime keypoint limitation and an unsupported ONNX opset for Mask R-CNN postprocessing.
The GPU verifier exposes one GPU to each test process. These results do not establish every multi-GPU training configuration.
The GPU suite does not cover every optional transformer path requiring timm; those paths retain their original optional dependency requirement.
GPU correctness and timing observations cover specific inputs, dtypes and model configurations on the available GPU, not long-run model convergence or universal performance.
Task modification benchmarks are disabled; downstream task-time and task-token savings were not measured.
Source-free authoring is a workflow boundary on a shared filesystem, not a separate security sandbox.
Prior semantic knowledge was reused only after verifying the same original commit; old candidate code and old test passes were not reused.

This was a supervised run: the host agent supplied source-free semantic clarifications and requested a necessary repair through official harness operations when the controller omitted the known optional-dependency regression. Controller and author model usage includes those executed repair calls; host supervision is excluded. This is not an unattended-harness performance benchmark.

An independent CPU float32 geometry probe reproduced numerical self-overlap and operand-order pathologies in both the original and candidate. All 12,288 observed values matched exactly. Compatibility with that behavior is preserved; these original numerical limitations are not claimed fixed.
